specification: M1 (severity.ladder), 35 covariates, n = 522, O < BC < KA

separation.method: severity.separation_diagnostics on each ordered-logit rung (flag if any |coef| or SE exceeds 10), zero cells in each binary covariate by outcome-class table, and a linear-programming separation check (ordinal and per cumulative split).

krinsky_robb.rule: full parameter vector drawn from the joint normal approximation on the estimation scale; sibling levels set to 0; 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles

design.cross_validation: 10 x 5 repeated stratified folds, seed 20260918, the splits of severity.cross_validated_log_loss; fold log loss is the mean negative log probability of the observed class, probabilities clipped at 1e-12

ordered_probit.note: slopes are on the probit scale; the AMEs are directly comparable

adjacent_category_logit.specification: log P(Y = j+1) / P(Y = j) = alpha_j + x'beta for j = O->BC and BC->KA, one slope vector shared by both adjacent pairs; a positive slope moves probability toward the more severe class. Custom maximum likelihood with the analytic score and the exact Hessian.

partial_proportional_odds_brant.why: covariates failing the per-covariate LR proportional-odds test at 5 percent, uncorrected (the severity.py rule; numbers.json severity.proportional_odds.failing)

convergence.optimizer_message: Desired error not necessarily achieved due to precision loss.

partial_proportional_odds_brant_noncross.why: the same model maximized subject to a non-negative middle-class probability on every row, so the likelihood is a proper one; the unconstrained fit has 6 rows whose cumulative probabilities cross

lr_vs_ordered_logit_M1.note: naive chi-squared reference; with active inequality constraints the reference distribution is not exactly chi-squared

partial_proportional_odds_brant_noncross.standard_errors: inverse numerical Hessian of the log-likelihood at the constrained optimum; with rows on the boundary these are approximate

partial_proportional_odds_holm.why: covariates failing after Holm correction (numbers.json severity.multiplicity.holm), the set BIC prefers to ordered logit

generalized_ordered_logit_noncrossing.why: the same model maximized subject to a non-negative middle-class probability on every row, so the likelihood is a proper one; the unconstrained fit has 10 rows whose cumulative probabilities cross

lr_vs_ordered_logit_M1.note: naive chi-squared reference; with active inequality constraints the reference distribution is not exactly chi-squared

generalized_ordered_logit_noncrossing.standard_errors: inverse numerical Hessian of the log-likelihood at the constrained optimum; with rows on the boundary these are approximate

design.model: ordered logit with cut_1n = c_1 + s_shift * nu_1 and cut_2n = cut_1n + exp(psi + s_gap * nu_2), nu ~ N(0, 1) per rider; variant 'increment' has s_shift = 0, variant 'both' estimates both. The random term on cut_1 moves both thresholds together; with no covariate in the thresholds it is a random intercept and is identified only through the shape of the logistic-normal mixture.
design.estimation: simulated maximum likelihood, scrambled Halton draws (random_parameters.halton_normal), analytic gradient, BFGS, covariance from central differences of the gradient
design.lr_reference: chi-bar-squared: equal mixture of chi2(0) and chi2(1) for one SD; 1/4, 1/2, 1/4 mixture of chi2(0), chi2(1), chi2(2) for two (random_parameters.lr_boundary)

convergence.message: Desired error not necessarily achieved due to precision loss.

firth.method: penalized likelihood l(theta) + 0.5 log det I(theta), I the expected information of the cumulative logit on (beta, cut_1, cut_2) (Jeffreys-prior penalty, Firth 1993). The cumulative logit is not a canonical link, so this penalized estimator is Firth-type but is not claimed to equal the adjusted-score mean-bias reduction of Kosmidis (2014). Standard errors are the inverse expected information at the penalized estimate; AME intervals use 1000 Krinsky-Robb draws.

raw_coding.prior: normal(0, 1) on every slope in the coding of the model frame (binary 0/1; poverty_share a 0-1 share; road density in km per 100 m buffer)

continuous_per_2sd.prior: normal(0, 1) on every slope with the continuous covariates (road_density_km_100m, poverty_share) measured per two standard deviations (Gelman et al. 2008), so a binary and a continuous slope get a prior of comparable strength

cue_block_power.design: Truth: the fitted M0c ordered logit (30 covariates) plus a common planted log-odds effect beta on each of the 5 admitted cues (sidewalk_transition, failure_to_yield, signal_violation, vehicle_turning_across, lane_positioning), applied to their observed values centered at the sample mean so the class balance stays near the observed 77/363/82 (centering only moves the thresholds). Outcomes simulated from the latent logistic model for the observed n = 522 rows and covariates. Each replication fits M0c and M1 by maximum likelihood (random_parameters.RPOrderedLogit with no random coefficient, BFGS, analytic gradient) and applies the 5-df likelihood-ratio test at 0.05. 200 replications per beta, seed default_rng([20261010, beta index, replication]). A replication counts only if both fits converge (max |gradient| < 1e-3).
cue_block_power.interpolation: linear between the bracketing grid points
